label: Expanded structural diagnosis of women’s marginalization into land-rights and green governance theory
description: Agarwal moved beyond employment statistics to prove that arable land ownership and commons governance are the decisive material anchors of South Asian women’s empowerment.
dialecticalTension: Shifts feminist development theory from wage labor to property rights and ecological governance.

citations.author: Bina Agarwal
citations.work: A Field of One's Own: Gender and Land Rights in South Asia

label: Replaced essentialist ecofeminist assumptions with materialist feminist environmentalism
description: While sharing ecological commitments, Agarwal critiqued cultural ecofeminism for romanticizing women’s biological closeness to nature instead of analyzing gendered property and labor.
dialecticalTension: Replaces essentialist nature-woman equation with materialist institutional analysis.

citations.author: Bina Agarwal
citations.work: The Gender and Environment Debate: Lessons from India

label: Pioneered feminist environmentalism grounded in empirical commons governance and property rights
description: Agarwal demonstrated empirically that women’s critical-mass participation in community forest governance improves both equity and ecological conservation.
dialecticalTension: Reconstructs ecofeminism on rigorous institutional and empirical foundations.
